graphics.caption: Folio 0030 Figure 1
graphics.title: Diagram of two intersecting circles ABC and DEF with assumed common centre K
graphics.description: Circles ABC and DEF intersecting at B and C, showing impossibility of common centre K.
graphics.text_reference: KB, KF, KG, have fallen on the circle DEF, the point K is the centre of the circle DEF. But K is also the centre of the circle ABC...

graphics.caption: Folio 0030 Figure 2
graphics.title: Diagram for Proposition 11 showing circles ABC and ADE touching internally at A
graphics.description: Circles ABC and ADE touching internally at A, showing line of centres FG must pass through A.
graphics.text_reference: I say that the straight line joined from G to F and produced will fall on A. For suppose it does not, but, if possible, let it fall as FGH...
